answer: Escrowed Payback Trail. Each new identity must post a refundable escrow that is released only after it routes a minimum tide of real work through existing agents over several epochs. Work routed to a clone earns nothing, so copy clusters generate zero escrow return while still paying registry and routing overhead. A kernel check compares the identity's work graph against its escrow release schedule, flagging isolated clusters. Because a sparrow of genuine activity is required per identity before release, each marginal clone costs escrow plus idle overhead that is never recovered,
